ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r5.claim: The Sidrat al-Muntaha is described as a lote tree in either the seventh or sixth heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r5.anchor: قيل: هي شجرة نبق في السماء السابعة. وقيل: في السماء السادسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r6.claim: Its fruit is compared to jars of Hajar, its leaves to elephant ears, and rivers mentioned by God flow from its base; a rider could travel in its shade for seventy years without crossing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r6.anchor: ثمرها كقلال هجر، وورقها كآذان الفيلة. تنبع من أصلها الأنهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r7.claim: One explanation of its name is that every scholar’s knowledge ends there, and only God knows what lies beyond it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r7.anchor: لأنه ينتهي إليها علم كل عالم، ولا يعلم ما وراءها صعدا إلا الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r8.claim: Other explanations make it the endpoint for believers’ souls, divine commands, angels ascending from heaven or earth, martyrs’ souls, Paradise, prophets and angels, prophetic knowledge, deeds, or those raised in honor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p13/r8.anchor: أو ينتهي إليها كل من مات على الإيمان من كل جيل أو ينتهي إليها ما نزل من أمر الله تعالى

NAHHAS:v4p270/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p270/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p270/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas asked Kaʿb about the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary; Kaʿb said it marks where scholars' knowledge ends and that only God knows what lies beyond.
NAHHAS:v4p270/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة عن ابن عباس سألت كعبا عن سدرة المنتهى فقال إليها ينتهي علم العلماء

NAHHAS:v4p270/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p270/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
NAHHAS:v4p270/r2.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says the Lote Tree is so named because the souls of believers reach it.
NAHHAS:v4p270/r2.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس سميت سدرة المنتهى لأنه تنتهي إليها أرواح المؤمنين

NAHHAS:v4p270/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p270/r3.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v4p270/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says everything belonging to God's command, from above or below, reaches the Lote Tree.
NAHHAS:v4p270/r3.anchor: ومذهب الضحاك أنه ينتهي إليها ما كان من أمر الله من فوقها أو من تحتها

NAHHAS:v4p270/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p270/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p270/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar considers all these explanations plausible; no report decisively settles the matter, and God knows best.
NAHHAS:v4p270/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وليس قول من هذه إلا وهو محتمل لذلك ولا خبر يقطع العذر

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.claim: Verses 13–18 refer to the Ascension and may belong to a later period than the early Makkan setting.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r2.anchor: Vv. 13–18, which refer to the Ascension of the Prophet, may, however, be from a later period

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.claim: Many commentators date the Ascension to the late Makkan period, most likely 619.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r3.anchor:
many commentators maintain that the Ascension of the Prophet Muhammad (miʿrāj
) did not occur until the late Makkan period, most likely in the year 619

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.speaker: a minority
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.claim: A minority dates the Ascension to 614, seven years before the hijrah.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r4.anchor: a minority maintain that it occurred seven years before the hijrah in 614

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.claim: The Prophet saw Gabriel another time at the Lote Tree of the Boundary.
ZAJJAJ:v5p72/r2.anchor: أي رآه مرة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى

RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.claim: The first sight on earth left only a remote possibility that the figure was a jinn, despite Muhammad’s necessary knowledge that he was an angel; seeing him at the Sidra above the sixth heaven excludes jinn or human presence.
RAZI-FULL:v28p250#3/r1.anchor: فلما رآه عند سدرة المنتهى وهو فوق السماء السادسة لم يحتمل أن يكون هناك جن ولا إنس

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r7.speaker: المشهور
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r7.claim: The famous view places the Sidrat al-Muntahā in the seventh heaven; another report places it in the sixth.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r7.anchor: المشهور أن السدرة شجرة في السماء السابعة

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet describes the tree’s fruit as jars from Hajar and its leaves as elephant ears; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r8.anchor: نيقها كقلال هجر وورقها كآذان الفيلة

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r9.claim: Another gloss makes the Sidra the utmost bewilderment, beyond which there is no bewilderment; Muhammad did not become bewildered or absent.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r9.anchor: وقيل سدرة المنتهى هي الحيرة القصوى من السدرة

RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r10.claim: “At” may denote place, meaning near the Sidra, or time, meaning the moment when the minds of the wise are at their most bewildered, though Muhammad was not bewildered then.
RAZI-FULL:v28p251/r10.anchor: المشهور أنه ظرف مكان تقديره رأى جبريل أو غيره بقرب سدرة المنتهى

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.claim: If the pronoun means God, reading “at the Sidra” as God’s location in a place is false; it can instead describe Muhammad as the one who was at the Sidra when he saw.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r1.anchor: قول من يجعل الله في مكان وهو باطل

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.claim: If the referent is Gabriel, either account of “at the Sidra” works, but Rāzī says Muhammad being there with Gabriel is clearer.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r2.anchor: وكون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع جبريل عند سدرة المنتهى أظهر

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r3.claim: The genitive may attach the tree to its place: the endpoint is a place no angel, or even spirit, passes beyond.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r3.anchor: إضافة الشيء إلى مكانه يقال أشجار بلدة كذا

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r4.claim: Alternatively, the genitive attaches a locus to what is in it: the tree is at the endpoint of knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r5.claim: A third reading makes it a possessive construction with the endpoint to God understood; association with God honors the tree.
RAZI-FULL:v28p252/r5.anchor: إضافة الملك إلى مالكه يقال دار زيد وأشجار زيد

STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.speaker: those who maintain the vision of God
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.claim: Proponents of the God-vision interpretation say the Prophet saw his Lord twice in special Self-Disclosure: above the Throne at the highest veil and at the Lote Tree of the Boundary.
STUDYQURAN:53:13/r3.anchor: Those who maintain that it refers to the vision of God say that the Prophet saw his Lord twice in a special Self-Disclosure

STUDYQURAN:53:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r1.claim: They place the lote tree in the seventh Heaven, to the right of the Divine Throne; it marks Paradise’s end or the limit of creation beyond which none passes or knows.
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r1.anchor: Most say it is a tree in the seventh Heaven to the right of the Divine Throne

STUDYQURAN:53:14/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r2.speaker: Ṭū
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r2.claim: Another view places the lote tree between the sixth and seventh heavens and takes the Garden of refuge as the seventh Heaven.
STUDYQURAN:53:14/r2.anchor: Others say the lote tree is at the boundary between the sixth and seventh heavens (Ṭū). In this interpretation, the Garden of the refuge is taken as a reference to the seventh Heaven

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r1.claim: Grammatically, ʿinda (“at”) attaches to raʾāhu (“he saw him”), though the cited locator in this segment is 27:40.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r1.anchor: عن قول الله: {عند سدرة المنتهى عندها جنة المأوى}

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r2.claim: The sidra is a nabq tree.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r2.anchor: وبالذي قلنا في أنها شجرة النبق تتابعت الأخبار عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقال أهل العلم

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r3.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r3.claim: Kaʿb says the tree is at the base of the Throne, where every scholar's knowledge ends, including that of a near angel or messenger prophet; what lies beyond is known only to God. A second account places it over the Throne-bearers and says creaturely knowledge ends there.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r3.anchor: إلى كعب الأحبار، فقال له حدثني عن قول الله: {عند سدرة المنتهى عندها جنة المأوى}

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r4.claim: Abdullah says that during the Night Journey the Prophet reached the sixth heaven's tree: those ascending from earth stop there, and what descends from above ends there.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r4.anchor: عن مرة، عن عبد الله قال: «لما أسري برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهي به إلى سدرة المنتهى وهي في السماء السادسة

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the tree is so named because nothing of God's command passes beyond it.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r5.anchor: قلت للضحاك: لم تسمى سدرة المنتهى؟ قال: «لأنه ينتهي إليها كل شيء من أمر الله لا يعدوها»

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r6.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says everyone who followed the Prophet's way reaches the tree, hence its name.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r6.anchor: عن الربيع، {عند سدرة المنتهى} [النجم: 14] قال: «إليها ينتهي كل أحد خلا على سنة أحمد، فلذلك سميت المنتهى»

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة أو غيره
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r7.claim: A report attributed uncertainly to Abu Hurayra or someone else says every member of Muhammad's community who followed his sunnah ends at the tree.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أو غيره شك أبو جعفر الرازي قال: لما أسري بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، انتهى إلى السدرة، فقيل له: «هذه السدرة ينتهي إليها كل أحد خلا من أمتك على سنتك»

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r8.claim: Al-muntaha means the endpoint; the tree may be named for knowledge ending there, for God's ascending and descending commands ending there, for followers of the prophetic way reaching it, or for all these reasons. No decisive report singles out one explanation.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r8.anchor: إنها سدرة في أصل العرش، إليها ينتهي علم كل عالم، ملك مقرب، أو نبي مرسل

TAB-FULL:v22p34/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r9.claim: Tabari says reports from the Messenger and scholars support identifying the sidra as a nabq tree.
TAB-FULL:v22p34/r9.anchor: وبالذي قلنا في أنها شجرة النبق تتابعت الأخبار عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وقال أهل العلم

TAB-FULL:v22p38/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r1.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's description: its fruits resembled jars and leaves elephant ears; when covered by God's command, it became ruby, emerald, and similar things.
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «انتهيت إلى السدرة فإذا نبقها مثل الجرار

TAB-FULL:v22p38/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r2.claim: In the report through Anas and Malik ibn Sasaa, the Prophet describes reaching the seventh heaven, meeting Abraham, then seeing Sidra fruit like Hajar pitchers and leaves like elephant ears.
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r2.anchor: عن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن أنس بن مالك، عن مالك بن صعصعة

TAB-FULL:v22p38/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r3.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet rode al-Buraq to the Sidra; its leaves were like elephant ears and fruit like pitchers, then its beauty became indescribable as God covered it and revealed what He revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ركبت البراق ثم ذهب بي إلى سدرة المنتهى

TAB-FULL:v22p38/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r4.claim: Anas reports that an angel carried the Prophet to the Sidra; he recognized its leaves and fruit, but divine covering transformed it beyond description.
TAB-FULL:v22p38/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عرج بي الملك» ؛ قال: «ثم انتهيت إلى السدرة

TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة، أو غيره
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r1.claim: A report whose attribution is uncertain (Abu Hurayra or another) says the Sidra marks the limit for each follower of the Prophet's Sunnah; rivers of pure water, milk, wine, and honey flow from it, and its vast shade and leaf encompass the ummah.
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أو غيره شك أبو جعفر الرازي

TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Sidra as at the center of Paradise, with abundant silk and brocade upon it.
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله

TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r3.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr reports the Prophet said a hundred riders could travel or take shade beneath one branch; it contains golden moths and pitcher-like fruit.
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r3.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وذكر سدرة المنتهى

TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v22p38#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas describes a tree whose shade takes a rider a hundred years to cross and whose leaf covers the entire community.

TAB-FULL:v22p39/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p39/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v22p39/r1.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's description of the Sidra in the seventh heaven: its fruit is like Hajar pitchers and its leaves like elephant ears; two rivers emerge openly and two are hidden, which Gabriel identifies as the Nile and Euphrates and rivers of Paradise respectively.
TAB-FULL:v22p39/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {عند سدرة المنتهى} [النجم: 14] : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BURSEVI:v9p184/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p184/r5.claim: The Sidrat al-Muntahā is a lote tree in the seventh heaven, to the right of the Throne; its fruit resembles large jars, its leaves elephant ears, rivers spring from its root, and its shade extends seventy years' travel.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r5.anchor: وهي شجرة نبق في السماء السابعة عن يمين العرش ثمرها كقلال هجر وورقها كآذان الفيلة

BURSEVI:v9p184/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p184/r6.claim: ʿInda may attach to raʾā or be a circumstantial phrase describing Gabriel, a created being seen at a particular place.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r6.anchor: وعند يجوز أن يكون متعلقا برأى وأن يكون حالا من المفعول المراد به جبرائيل

BURSEVI:v9p184/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
BURSEVI:v9p184/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes al-muntahā as a verbal noun meaning ending, or as a place noun for the terminal point, as if it stood at the end of Paradise.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r7.anchor: والمنتهى مصدر ميمي بمعنى الانتهاء كما قال الزمخشري أو اسم مكان بمعنى موضع الانتهاء

BURSEVI:v9p184/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r8.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p184/r8.claim: One view says angels end there and cannot pass it; Gabriel's station is exclusive, just as the community may share Eden without reaching the Prophet's special station.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r8.anchor: وقيل : ينتهي إليها الملائكة ولا يتجاوزونها لأن جبرائيل رسول الملائكة إذا لم يتجاوزها

BURSEVI:v9p184/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r9.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p184/r9.claim: Another view says creaturely knowledge and deeds terminate there: ordinary good deeds reach it through angels, while the most sincere deeds of the elect pass beyond angelic conveyance into the spiritual realm, known only to God.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r9.anchor: وقيل إليها ينتهي علم الخلائق وأعمالهم ولا يعلم أحدا ما وراءها وذلك لأن الأعمال الصالحة في عليين

BURSEVI:v9p184/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p184/r10.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v9p184/r10.claim: Other explanations place the endpoint of martyrs' souls there, or say rulings descend from above while effects ascend from below.
BURSEVI:v9p184/r10.anchor: وقيل : ينتهي إليها أرواح الشهداء لأنها في أرض الجنان أو ينتهي إليها ما يهبط من فوقها من الأحكام

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r5.claim: On that reading, “at the Lote Tree” modifies the seeing, not the descent, and Gabriel is seen in his original form there.

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r7.claim: Sidr is a known tree, tāʾ marks a single tree, and muntahā appears to name a place, likely the end of the heavens because the Garden is beside it.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r7.anchor: السدر شجر معروف والتاء للوحدة والمنتهى - كأنه - اسم مكان

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r8.claim: God does not explain what the tree is; its deliberate obscurity is reinforced by the next phrase saying only that something covers it.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r8.anchor: ولا يوجد في كلامه تعالى ما يفسر هذه الشجرة

TABATABAI:53:1-18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r9.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r9.claim: Reports describe the tree as above the seventh heaven, where the deeds of Adam's descendants terminate.
TABATABAI:53:1-18/r9.anchor: شجرة فوق السماء السابعة إليها تنتهي أعمال بني آدم

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r1.claim: In the continuation of the Companions’ question, the Prophet says he reached the Lote Tree, whose leaf shaded a community, and was as near to his Lord as two bows or closer.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r1.anchor: انتهيت إلى سدرة المنتهى وإذا الورقة منها تظل أمة من الأمم فكنت من ربي كقاب قوسين أو أدنى

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r2.speaker: أنس
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet describing Sidra berries as locusts and leaves as elephant ears; when God’s command covered it, it changed into ruby, emerald, and similar things.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r2.anchor: أخرج أحمد وابن جرير عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r3.claim: In a report from Abu Ja‘far, Gabriel stops at Sidra, tells the Prophet to proceed to a station no creature reached before, and the Prophet sees divine light while majesty intervenes between him and God.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث طويل فلما انتهى به إلى سدرة المنتهى

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r4.claim: Al-Tabatabai explains al-sabha as majesty: it signifies God’s transcendence from creation and therefore points back to that primary sense.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r4.anchor: السبحة الجلال كما فسر في الرواية

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r5.claim: The report’s conclusion means that the Prophet saw his Lord through the vision of God’s signs.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r5.anchor: ومحصل ذيل الرواية أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم رأى ربه برؤية آياته

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi places the second vision at Sidra in the seventh heaven.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r6.anchor: في قوله تعالى { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى } قال في السماء السابعة

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.claim: Al-Tabatabai directs readers to his earlier account of the Mi‘raj reports in the opening commentary on Surat al-Isra, where he reviewed their differing descriptions.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم في أول تفسير سورة الإسراء روايات جامعة لقصة معراجه

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.claim: The earlier discussion recorded disagreement over whether the Mi‘raj occurred in a dream or while awake, and whether an awake ascent involved body and soul or the soul alone.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r9.anchor: الاختلاف في كيفية معراجه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه كان في المنام أو في اليقظة

TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.claim: Explaining the ascent as night travel to other planets, star systems, or galaxies conflicts with the detailed reports and has no coherent fit with the verses.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#3/r15.anchor: فمما لا يلائمه الأخبار الواردة في تفصيل القصة البتة بل ولا محصل مضامين الآيات المتقدمة

TABRISI:53:14-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
TABRISI:53:14-18/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil place the Lote Tree right of the Throne above the seventh heaven, where each angel's knowledge ends.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r1.anchor: وهي شجرة عن يمين العرش فوق السماء السابعة انتهى إليها علم كل ملك عن الكلبي ومقاتل

TABRISI:53:14-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود والضحاك
TABRISI:53:14-18/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Dahhak say it is the boundary for what ascends to heaven and God's commands descending from above it.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r2.anchor: إليها ينتهي ما يعرج إلى السماء وما يهبط من فوقها من أمر الله عن ابن مسعود والضحاك

TABRISI:53:14-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:14-18/r3.claim: One view says the souls of martyrs reach the Lote Tree.

TABRISI:53:14-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:14-18/r4.claim: Another account says descending things and ascending spirits are received there.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r4.anchor: ما يهبط به من فوقها ويقبض منها وإليها ينتهي ما يعرج من الأرواح

TABRISI:53:14-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:14-18/r5.claim: Muntahā is the place of ending; the tree is named for the angels' stopping point.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r5.anchor: والمنتهى موضع الانتهاء وهذه الشجرة حيث انتهى إليه الملائكة فأضيفت إليه

TABRISI:53:14-18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:14-18/r6.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:53:14-18/r6.claim: An alternative identifies it as the Tree of Ṭūbā; the sidra is also called the tree of prophecy.
TABRISI:53:14-18/r6.anchor: هي شجرة طوبى عن مقاتل والسدرة هي شجرة النبوة

THALABI:v9p142/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p142/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p142/r3.claim: The preposition ʿinda is syntactically attached to the verb ‘he saw him.’
THALABI:v9p142/r3.anchor: عند سدرة المنتهى (عند) صلة من قوله: رآه

THALABI:v9p142/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p142/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p142/r4.claim: The sidra is a nabq tree, called the Lote Tree of the Limit because the knowledge of every knower ends there.
THALABI:v9p142/r4.anchor: والسدرة: شجرة النبق، وقيل لها سدرة المنتهى لأنه إليها ينتهي علم كل عالم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r1.claim: Sidr is a kind of lote tree, and al-muntaha means the place where things end.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r1.anchor: والسدر في اللغة: ضرب من شجر النبق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r2.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas says it is called the Lote Tree of the Boundary because the angels' knowledge ends there; none passes beyond it except the Messenger when the rifraf descended to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: وإنما سميت سدرة المنتهى؛ لأن علم الملائكة ينتهي إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil place the tree to the right of the Throne above the seventh heaven, where every angel's knowledge ends.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي، ومقاتل: هي شجرة عن يمين العرش فوق السماء السابعة انتهى إليها علم كل ملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r4.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r4.claim: Abdullah says it is named because everything descending from above or ascending from below by God's command ends there and does not pass it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله: سميت سدرة المنتهى؛ لأنه ينتهي إليها ما يهبط من فوقها وما يصعد من تحتها من أمر الله تعالى لا يعدوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra says that on the Night Journey, the Prophet reached a tree where every follower of his Sunna would end; it had rivers flowing from its base and was so vast that a rider could travel a hundred years in its shade and one leaf could cover the whole community.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r6.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r6.claim: Abdullah says the tree bears additional silk and brocade.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الله: هي شجرة عليها فضول السندس والإستبرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r7.speaker: أنس عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r7.claim: Anas reports that during the Prophet's ascent to the seventh heaven, the tree's fruits were like jars from Hajar, its leaves like elephant ears, and it had two visible rivers and two hidden rivers; Gabriel identified the hidden ones as rivers in Paradise and the visible ones as the Nile and Euphrates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r7.anchor: وروى قتادة عن أنس، أن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r8.claim: Muqatil identifies the two hidden rivers in the report as Salsabil and Kawthar.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r9.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس وكعب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r9.claim: Ikrima reports Ibn Abbas asking Ka'b what the tree is; Ka'b says it is where angelic knowledge and God's command end and angelic knowledge does not pass beyond.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r9.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: سألت كعبا: ما سدرة المنتهى؟ قال: سدرة ينتهي إليها علم الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r10.claim: The tree is called al-muntaha because it stands at the place where angels and prophets reach their limit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p30/r10.anchor: ومعنى المنتهى موضع الانتهاء، وهذه الشجرة هناك وعندها تنتهي الملاكة والنبيون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r1.claim: The Lote Tree is where created beings' knowledge ends; what lies beyond is unseen and known only to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:14-17/r1.anchor: وهي شجرة إليها ينتهي علم الخلق، وما وراءها غيب لا يعلمه إلا الله عز وجل

QASHANI:53:13-15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:13-15/r2.speaker: قيل
QASHANI:53:13-15/r2.claim: One reported view identifies the Lote Tree as a tree in the seventh heaven where angelic knowledge ends and none knows what lies beyond; it is the Garden's furthest station and the refuge of martyrs' spirits.
QASHANI:53:13-15/r2.anchor: قيل: هي شجرة في السماء السابعة ينتهي إليها علم الملائكة

QASHANI:53:13-15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:13-15/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:13-15/r3.claim: The Lote Tree signifies the greatest spirit, with no determination or rank beyond it except pure ipseity; it is the return point from absolute annihilation to subsistence.
QASHANI:53:13-15/r3.anchor: فهي الروح الأعظم الذي لا تعين وراءها ولا مرتبة ولا شيء فوقها إلا الهوية المحضة

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.claim: Elmalili rejects Gabriel as the descending figure because Gabriel cannot pass the Sidra, so the location beside it does not fit a descent by him from above.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r11.anchor: Lâkin Cibrîl Sidre-i Müntehâ’dan öte geçemediğine göre

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r14.claim: Sidrat al-Muntaha is a genitive construction; muntaha can be a place noun or a mim verbal noun, meaning the sidra at the final limit or of the ultimate boundary.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r14.anchor: “Sidre-i Müntehâ”, Müntehâ Sidresi, terkîb-i izâfîdir. “Müntehâ” ism-i mekân ve masdar-ı mîmî olabileceğine göre

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r15.claim: The Kāmus entry identifies sidr as the nabq or Arabian cherry tree, lists its plurals and distinguishes garden and wild varieties, with sweet versus tart fruit and dense, pleasant shade.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r15.anchor: sîn’in kesri ve dâl’in sükûnuyla şecer-i nebk ismidir ki ‘Arabistan kirazı’ tâbir olunur. Trabzon hurması ol nevidendir.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r16.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r16.claim: Seder can mean dazzlement or bewilderment, and sidra as a noun of type can suggest astonishment; commentators use this alongside the tree sense.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r16.anchor: “Seder” ve “sederât” göz kamaşmak ve hayran olmak demektir.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r17.claim: The popular account places the tree at the right of the Throne in the seventh heaven, though a hadith says the sixth; rivers of the Paradise promised to the pious flow beneath it.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r17.anchor: Sidre-i Müntehâ, Arş’ın sağından yedinci semâda -bir hadiste de altıncı semâda- bir nebk ağacıdır

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r18.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r18.claim: Prophetic reports describe a tree whose shade a rider could traverse for seventy years, or in another version a hundred, and whose leaf could cover the entire community.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r19.claim: Elmalili sees the tree as an image of the created world's ultimate formation, marking the boundary of formed bodies and dimensions where the realm of command begins.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r19.anchor: Bunda bütün âlem-i halkın ecrâm ve eb‘âdı ile müntehâ-yı teşekkülâtı, âlem-i emir hudûduna dikilmiş bir ağaç

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r20.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r20.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Sidra at Paradise's extremities, with hems of fine silk and brocade over it; Kashshaf accordingly calls it at Paradise's end.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r20.anchor: Mes‘ûd radıyallâhu anh’tan da: الْجَن َّةِ عَلَيـْهَا فُضُولُ

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r21.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b say the Sidra is beneath the Throne, where knowledge of every angel, prophet, and other creature ends; what lies beyond is known only to God.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r21.anchor: İbn Abbas ve Ka‘b’dan nakledildiğine göre Sidre-i Müntehâ Arş’ın tahtında bir sidredir ki gerek melek ve gerek nebî

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r22.speaker: Dahhâk
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r22.claim: Dahhak's reported view is that every matter from the divine command reaches the Sidra and goes no farther.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r22.anchor: emr-i ilâhîden her şey ona müntehî olur. Ondan ileri geçmez.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r23.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r23.claim: Razi records an alternative that sidra is a noun of one occurrence from rider/rikba, so the phrase means supreme astonishment; the Prophet was not bewildered or disoriented.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r23.anchor: Fahr-i Râzî’nin birinciden sonra kaydettiği bir kavle göre de; “sidre” “râkib”den “rikbe” gibi binâ-i merre olarak Sidre-i Müntehâ hayret-i kusvâ demektir.

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r24.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r24.claim: Razi explicitly says the first interpretation, the physical sidra, is the sound one.
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r24.anchor: Râzî der ki “sahih olan evvelki vecihtir.”

ELMALILI:53:11-14/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r25.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:53:11-14/r25.claim: Abu Suud suggests muntaha may mean God, by 53:42, so Sidrat al-Muntaha is God's sidra, as property is attributed to its owner.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.claim: The mysterious, vivid scene points to faith about what senses cannot reach and warns against straining reason beyond its limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.anchor: duyularla algılanamayan, fizik âlemin ötesine taşan konularda imanın esas olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.claim: The passage condemns pagan attempts to make divinity concrete through material or spiritual intermediaries and to ascribe godhood to beings besides God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka varlıklara tanrılık izâfe etme telakkisini mahkûm etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.claim: Although the sūra is early Meccan, these verses, especially 13–18, are generally understood as relating to the Miʿrāj near the end of the Meccan period.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r3.anchor: 13-18. âyetlerin, Mekke döneminin sonlarına doğru gerçekleştiği bilinen mi‘rac olayı ile ilgili olduğu kabul edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.claim: If the scene is the Miʿrāj, appearance, horizon, Sidra, descent, and nearness are figurative descriptions of divine acts and attributes, understood without asking how or how much.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.anchor: “görünme, yüce ufukta, sidretü’l-müntehâda olma, inme, çok yaklaşma” gibi ifadeleri mecazi mânada almak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r41.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r41.claim: Sidrat al-Muntahā marks the boundary of what created beings can know, a station that intensifies awe beyond imagination.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r41.anchor: yaratılmışlarca bilinebilirlerin son sınırını işaretlediği kabul edilen hudut noktası; akıllara durgunluk verecek ölçüde hayreti arttıran makam

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r42.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r42.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r42.claim: The tree sense of sidra and reports placing the Sidra at Paradise’s edge are compatible with this boundary interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r42.anchor: sidre kelimesinin bir ağaç türünü ifade etmesinden ve “sidretü’l-müntehâ”nın cennetin uçlarında olduğunu belirten rivayetlerden hareketle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.claim: Elmalılı’s summary says Gabriel appeared in whatever form he took during each Qur’anic revelation, but in his true form only once before the Miʿrāj and once while descending from it, meeting the Prophet at the Sidra.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r57.anchor: Resûlullah, Cebrâil’i Kur’an’ın her inen parçası esnasında, hangi sûrete girmişse öyle görüyordu

BURHAN:v4p290/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r4.claim: ʿInd and ladā can denote literal nearness, as in the Prophet’s sighting at the Lote Tree and Joseph’s master at the door.

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r17.claim: The Lote Tree is in Paradise and marks the limit of the angels.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r17.anchor: وهي شجرة في الجنة ، وهي منتهى الملائكة

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r18.claim: Other views say the tree is where the souls of martyrs, or the souls of all creatures, end; no one knows what lies beyond it except God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r18.anchor: تنتهي إليها أرواح الخلق ، ولا يعلم ما وراءها إلا الله تعالى

ITQAN:v2p482/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r1.claim: ʿInda is a locative adverb for physical presence or nearness and for figurative nearness, which in such verses means honor and elevated rank.
ITQAN:v2p482/r1.anchor: ظرف مكان تستعمل في الحضور والقرب سواء كانا حسيين نحو ﴿ فلما رآه مستقرا عنده ﴾

SULAMI:v2p285#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r1.claim: The Prophet did not prostrate at the Sidra out of reverence for its station and the intimacy and nearness there; he will prostrate at the Resurrection for intercession, where need calls for supplication.
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : لم يسجد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عند سدرة المنتهى تعظيما للمحل ولما كان فيه

SULAMI:v2p285#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r2.claim: Unveiling of distress reaches the Sidra except for the Prophet, who once attained the Sidra and whose sight did not swerve or overstep.
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا : إلى سدرة المنتهى يبلغ كشف الهموم إلا لرجل واحد وهو الذي ﴿ دنا فتدلى ﴾ مرة على سدرة المنتهى

SULAMI:v2p285#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r3.claim: The Prophet did not turn back to witness himself; he was wholly witnessing his Lord and what appeared to him of the attributes that established him in that station.
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r3.anchor: قال سهل : لم يرجع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى شاهد نفسه ولا إلى مشاهدتها وإنما كان مشاهدا بكليته لربه

SULAMI:v2p285#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtaʾ says the Prophet saw without excess or deviation, with the faculties in due balance and without doubt.
SULAMI:v2p285#5/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء لم يره بطغيان يميل بل رآه على شروط اعتدال القوى فلا شك فيه ولا امتراء

ITQAN:v1p73/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p73/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v1p73/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi classifies Qur'anic revelation as celestial, terrestrial, between heaven and earth, and even beneath the earth in a cave.
ITQAN:v1p73/r1.anchor: تقدم قول ابن العربي إن من القرآن سمائيا وأرضيا

ITQAN:v1p73/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p73/r2.speaker: هبة الله المفسر
ITQAN:v1p73/r2.claim: A report says revelation generally came between Mecca and Medina, except six verses said to have descended neither on earth nor in heaven: three from al-Saffat, one from al-Zukhruf, and the final two of al-Baqara on the Night Journey.
ITQAN:v1p73/r2.anchor: أنبأنا هبة الله المفسر قال نزل القرآن بين مكة والمدينة إلا ست آيات

ITQAN:v1p73/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p73/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v1p73/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi suggests the extraordinary verses meant those revealed in the space between heaven and earth; he says Surat al-Mursalat came beneath the earth in the cave, based on a sound report from Ibn Masʿud.
ITQAN:v1p73/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي ولعله أراد في الفضاء بين السماء والأرض

ITQAN:v1p73/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p73/r4.claim: Al-Suyuti finds no support for the unusual-location claims about the earlier verses except the final al-Baqara verses; he cites Muslim's Ibn Masʿud report that at Sidrat al-Muntaha the Prophet received five prayers, the final verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for major sins by those avoiding shirk.
ITQAN:v1p73/r4.anchor: قلت أما الآيات المتقدمة فلم أقف على مستند لما ذكره فيها

ITQAN:v1p73/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p73/r5.speaker: الهذلي
ITQAN:v1p73/r5.claim: Al-Hudhali's al-Kamil says the final verses beginning Amana al-Rasul were revealed at the distance of two bow lengths.
ITQAN:v1p73/r5.anchor: وفي الكامل للهذلي نزلت ﴿ آمن الرسول ﴾ إلى آخرها بقاب قوسين

TUSTARI:53:14/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:53:14/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:53:14/r1.claim: The Lote Tree of the Boundary is the tree at which everyone's knowledge ends.
TUSTARI:53:14/r1.anchor: وهي شجرة ينتهي إليها علم كل أحد

DAMGHANI:v1p335/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r1.claim: ʿInda can mean near or beside; the tree and Garden of Abode are described as near one another.
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r1.anchor: بالقرب والمجاورة قوله تعالى في سورة النجم عند سدرة المنتهى يعني بقرب سدرة المنتهى عندها جنة الماوى يعني بقربها ومجاورتها

SAMIN-DURR:53:14-15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:14-15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:14-15/r1.claim: عند سدرة is an adverb modifying رآه.

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r1.claim: Asad identifies the lote-tree scene with Muhammad's mystic experience of the Ascension (mi'raj).
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r1.anchor: on the occasion of his mystic experience of the "Ascension" (mi'raj).

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r2.speaker: Raghib
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r2.claim: Raghib takes the leafy lote tree as a symbol of paradise's shade, meaning spiritual peace and fulfillment.
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r2.anchor: Raghib suggests that owing to the abundance of its leafy shade, the sidr or sidrah

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r3.claim: The term al-muntaha suggests that God sets a limit to created knowledge: humans cannot grasp ultimate reality, even in paradise, which God reserves for Himself.
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n10/r3.anchor: God has set a definite limit to all knowledge accessible to created beings

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p48/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p48/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p48/r3.claim: If the star's falling is meant, it evokes prostration toward earth; that nearness in worship mirrors the Prophet's ascent to the lote tree at the closest journey to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p48/r3.anchor: وكأنما النجم هوى ليسجد لله تعالى والسجود أقرب ما يكون إلى الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r2.claim: The use of ʿalā with the vision contrasts with fī in the previous verse: the vision itself is not the subject of dispute, unlike reports about the unseen Hour.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r2.anchor: والملاحظ هنا استخدام حرف (على) أما في الآية السابقة استخدم الحرف (في)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r5.claim: Al-muntahā means the last or furthest point, which is located by the Garden of Abode.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p55/r5.anchor: المنتهى هي آخر شيء وآخر نقطة ومكانها عند جنة المأوى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p814/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p814/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p814/r3.claim: God spoke to Moses at the sacred valley and on Sinai, the highest place Moses reached; Muhammad ascended to the higher Sidrat al-Muntaha, so God gave him the grounds for belief and removed the disbelievers' objection.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p814/r3.anchor: وأعلى مكان كلّم الله تعالى موسى عليه هو الطور

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's description of the Lote Tree at the seventh heaven: its fruit resembled Hajar jars, its leaves elephant ears, and four rivers flowed from its trunk; Gabriel identified the hidden two as in Paradise and the visible two as the Nile and Euphrates.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r1.anchor: عن أنس في قوله تعالى ﴿ عند سدرة المنتهى ﴾ أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال رفعت لي سدرة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Banū Hāshim view was that Muhammad had seen his Lord twice.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r2.anchor: قال أما نحن بنو هاشم نزعم أو نقول إن محمدا قد رأى ربه مرتين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r3.speaker: كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r3.claim: Kaʿb says God divided vision and speech between Muhammad and Moses: Moses spoke with God, while Muhammad saw Him with his heart.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r3.anchor: قال فكبر كعب حتى جاوبته الجبال ثم قال إن الله قسم رؤيته وكلامه بين محمد وموسى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r4.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha rejects the claim that Muhammad saw his Lord, saying he saw Gabriel in his own form; she also denies that anyone knows the five unseen matters, citing 31:34.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r4.anchor: فأخبرني مسروق أنه قال لعائشة قلت أي أمتاه هل رأى محمد ربه فقالت إنك لتقول قولا إنه ليقف منه شعري

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r5.speaker: معمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r5.claim: Maʿmar says that in their view ʿĀʾisha was not more knowledgeable than Ibn ʿAbbās, taking issue with her account of the vision.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r5.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق فذكرت هذا الحديث لمعمر فقال ما عائشة عندنا بأعلم من ابن عباس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan used to swear that Muhammad saw his Lord.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p251#3/r6.anchor: عن المبارك بن فضالة قال كان الحسن يحلف بالله لقد رأى محمد ربه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p5#2/r8.claim: The sidrah is a lote tree.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r1.claim: On the well-known view, the Sidrat al-Muntaha is a real lote tree to the right of the Throne in the seventh heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r1.anchor: هيشجرة نبق عن يمين العرش في السماء السابعى على المشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r2.claim: Reports in Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi describe its fruit as jars from Hajar and leaves as elephant ears, with shade a rider cannot cross in seventy years.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r2.anchor: وفي حديث أخرجه أحمد ومسلم والترمذي وغيرهم في السماء نبقها كقلال هجر وأوراقها مثل آذان الفيلة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r3.claim: Al-Hakim authenticates a report from Asma bint Abi Bakr that a rider would travel among its branches for one hundred years.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا يسير الراكب في الفنن منها مائة سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r4.claim: These reports indicate a literal lote tree; God can create vegetation wherever He wills, as with the zaqqum tree at Hell's root (37:64).
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r4.anchor: والأحاديث ظاهرة في أنها شجرة نبق حقيقة والنبات في الشاهد يكون ترابيا ومائيا وهوائيا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r5.claim: An alternative treats sidra metaphorically because angels gather there as people gather under a tree's shade.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r5.anchor: السدرة عليها مجاز لأنها تجتمع عندها الملائكة عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r6.claim: Al-Muntaha is a place noun, though it may also be a mīmī verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r6.anchor: و ( المنتهى ) اسم مكان وجوز كونه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is where the knowledge of every scholar ends, beyond which only God knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس إليها ينتهي علم كل عالم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r8.claim: Some say prophetic knowledge ends there.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r8.anchor: أو لأنها ينتهي إليها علم الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r9.claim: Other views say deeds of creatures are presented there, or descending and ascending things and spirits terminate there.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r9.anchor: أو لأنها تنتهي إليها أعمال الخلائق بأن تعرض على الله تعالى عندها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r10.claim: A further explanation makes it the endpoint of those raised there in honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r10.anchor: أو لانتهاء من رفع إليها في الكرامة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r11.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf describes the tree as the boundary and farthest end of Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r11.anchor: وفي الكشاف كأنها منتهى الجنة وآخرها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r12.claim: The annexation may join a thing to its location or a location to what it contains.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r12.anchor: إضافة ( سدرة ) إلى ( المنتهى ) من إضافة الشيء لمحله كما في أشجار البستان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r13.claim: A far-fetched view identifies al-Muntaha with God, making the phrase God's tree, the One to whom is the ultimate end (53:42).
ALUSI-FULL:v27p50#2/r13.anchor: المراد بالمنتهى الله عز وجل فالإضافة من إضافة الملك إلى المالك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the Sidra is in the seventh heaven; everything ascending from earth and descending from above ends there; what covered it was golden moths.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r2.anchor: انتهى إلى سدرة المنتهى وهي في السماء السابعة إليها ينتهي ما يعرج به من الأرض فيقبض منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r3.claim: In the Miʿraj report, the Prophet describes meeting Abraham in the seventh heaven and seeing the Sidra's fruit like jars from Hajar and leaves like elephant ears.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r3.anchor: ثم صعد بي إلى السماء السابعة فإذا أنا بإبراهيم عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r4.claim: The Sidra is a lote tree; it is called the Utmost Boundary because creation's knowledge ends there.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r4.anchor: "والسدرة" شجرة النبق، وقيل لها: سدرة المنتهى لأنه إليها ينتهي علم الخلق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r5.speaker: كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r5.claim: Kaʿb says the tree stands at the base of the Throne above its bearers; creaturely knowledge ends there, and what lies beyond is unseen to all but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r5.anchor: فقال كعب: إنها سدرة في أصل العرش على رؤوس حملة العرش وإليها ينتهي علم الخلائق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r6.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr reports the Prophet's description of a branch whose shade accommodates a rider for a hundred years and a hundred thousand riders, with fruit like jars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r6.anchor: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذكر سدرة المنتهى، قال: "يسير الراكب في ظل الفنن منها مائة عام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r7.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r7.claim: Muqatil describes a tree bearing ornaments, garments, and fruit of every color; a leaf placed on earth would illuminate it, and identifies it with Tuba in al-Raʿd.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p404#3/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: هي شجرة تحمل الحلي والحلل والثمار من جميع الألوان

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r7.claim: The Lote Tree marks the limit reached by creatures' deeds and knowledge, or by what descends from above and ascends from below it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r7.anchor: التي ينتهي إليها أعمال الخلائق وعلمهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.claim: It may be likened to a lote tree because people gather in its shade.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r8.anchor: ولعلها شبهت بالسدرة وهي شجرة النبق لأنهم يجتمعون في ظلها

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet places the Lote Tree in the seventh heaven.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:12-14/r9.anchor: وروي مرفوعا أنها في السماء السابعة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r8.claim: The sidrah is a lote-like tree at the limit of created knowledge, where what ascends from below and descends from above is received.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r8.anchor: { عند سدرة المنتهى * } أي الشجرة التي هي كالسدر وينتهي إليها علم الخلائق وينتهي إليها ما يعرج من تحت

BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.claim: He places the second descent at the Night Journey, shortly before the Hijra in the thirteenth year of prophethood, after ascent through the stations, where the pen-scratching was heard.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p319/r9.anchor: وذلك - والله أعلم - ليلة الإسراء في السنة الثالثة عشرة من النبوة قبل الهجرة بقليل بعد الترقي في معراج الكمالات

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.claim: The Prophet’s pardon of his Meccan kin at the conquest echoes Joseph’s pardon of his brothers; the source quotes Joseph’s words as the model.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r1.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم } ) 77

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r2.claim: Meeting Idris in the fourth heaven foreshadows the Prophet’s elevated station: Idris was the first given writing by the pen, and Muhammad later wrote to kings calling them to obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r2.anchor: ثم لقاؤه إدريس عليه السلام في السماء الرابعة وهو المكان الذي سماه الله مكانا عليا وإدريس أول من آتاه الله الخط بالقلم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r3.speaker: أبو سفيان
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r3.claim: The source quotes Abu Sufyan at Heraclius, who remarked that Muhammad’s command had made even the Byzantine king fear him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r3.anchor: حتى قال أبو سفيان وهو عند ملك الروم حين جاء كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ورأى ما رأى من خوف هرقل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r4.claim: The kings’ responses to Muhammad’s letters mirrored his victory: the Negus and Oman’s ruler followed him, Heraclius and al-Muqawqis made peace and sent gifts, and resisters were overcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r4.anchor: فمنهم من اتبعه على دينه كالنجاشي وملك بني عمان ومنهم من هادئه وأهدى إليه وأتحفه كهرقل والمقوقس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r5.claim: Meeting Aaron in the fifth heaven foreshadows the love Muhammad would gain among Quraysh and the Arabs after some initially opposed him.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r5.anchor: ولقاؤه في السماء الخامسة لهارون عليه السلام المحبب في قومه يؤذن بحب قريش وجميع العرب له بعد بعضهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r6.claim: Meeting Moses in the sixth heaven foreshadows a campaign in Syria and return to the land of departure: the source links this to Tabuk, the captured ruler of Duma’s tribute settlement, and the conquest of Mecca.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r6.anchor: ولقاؤه في السماء السادسة لموسى عليه السلام يؤذن بحالة تشبه حالة موسى عليه السلام حين أمر بغزو الشام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r7.claim: Abraham at the seventh heaven, beside al-Bayt al-Maʿmur, points to pilgrimage: angels visit it as Abraham built the Kaʿba and called people to Hajj; Muhammad’s final state was Hajj with about seventy thousand Muslims.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r7.anchor: ثم لقاؤه في السماء السابعة إبراهيم عليه السلام لحكمتين : إحداهما أنه رآه عند البيت المعمور مسندا ظهره إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r8.claim: The Night Journey’s culmination is pure monotheism, represented by the prescribed prayer as the barrier between Islam and polytheism and as a comprehensive source of religious blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r8.anchor: وهذا المقام هو الإسراء وما تفرع منه الموصل إلى أعلى ما يكون من تجريد التوحيد , فجعل سبحانه عنوانه المفروض فيه الحاجز بين الإسلام والشرك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r9.claim: Prayer was first prescribed as fifty daily prayers, then reduced to five with a much lighter burden but the reward of fifty; congregational prayer counts as twenty-seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r9.anchor: بأن جعلت خمسين مستغرقة لجميع الفراغ ثم ردت إلى خمس دون القوى بكثير ثم رتب عليها جزاء الخمسين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r10.claim: The two endpoint prayers, dawn and afternoon, receive special merit because angels of both shifts witness and record them in each group’s register.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r10.anchor: وفضل صلاتي الطرفين : الصبح الثنائية والعصر الرباعية بشهادة فريقي الملائكة وكتبتهما في صحيفتي كل من الجمعين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r11.speaker: حمزة الكرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r11.claim: In Jawāmiʿ al-Tafsīr, al-Kirmani says the Night Journey occurred from Umm Hani’s house in Rabiʿ I before the Hijra, then gives a lengthy account.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p321/r11.anchor: فقال حمزة الكرماني في جوامع التفسير : فأسري به في شهر ربيع الأول قبل الهجرة من بيت أم هانىء

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says the Sidrah is in the sixth heaven, where ascending spirits and what descends from above terminate; it was covered by golden moths.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r12.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: لما أسري برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهى به إلى سدرة المنتهى وهي في السماء السادسة إليها ينتهي ما يعرج من الأرواح

DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r13.claim: The same report says the Prophet received the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for members of his community who die without associating partners with God, even with grave sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p648#2/r13.anchor: قال: وأعطي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثا: أعطي الصلوات الخمس وأعطي خواتيم سورة البقرة وغفر لمن لا يشرك بالله شيئا من أمته المقحمات

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the knowledge of every scholar ends at the Sidrah; what lies beyond is known only to God.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل عن سدرة المنتهى قال: إليها ينتهي علم كل عالم وما وراءها لا يعلمه إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains its name by saying every matter from God ends there and does not pass beyond it.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك أنه قيل له: لم تسمى سدرة المنتهى قال: لأنه ينتهي إليها كل شيء من أمر الله لا يعدوها

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r3.claim: In a report through Shamr, Ibn Abbas hears from Kaʿb that the Sidrah is at the root of the Throne; the knowledge of every near angel and messenger prophet ends there, and beyond is unseen known only to God.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r3.anchor: عن شمر قال: جاء ابن عباس إلى كعب فقال: حدثني عن سدرة المنتهي قال: إنها سدرة في أصل العرش إليها ينتهي علم كل ملك مقرب أو نبي مرسل

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r4.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r4.claim: Kaʿb places the Sidrah above the Throne-bearers; creaturely knowledge ends there, which explains its name.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r4.anchor: عن كعب قال: إنها سدرة على رؤوس حملة العرش إليها ينتهي علم الخلائق ثم ليس لأحد وراءها علم فلذلك سميت سدرة المنتهى

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Kaʿb's view that angelic knowledge ends at the Sidrah, where the angels receive God's command, with no knowledge beyond it.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سألت كعبا ما سدرة المنتهى قال: سدرة ينتهي إليها علم الملائكة وعندها يجدون أمر الله لا يجاوزها علم

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r7.claim: Ibn Masud locates the Sidrah at the center of Paradise, with extra silk and brocade spread over it.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {عند سدرة المنتهى} قال: صبو الجنة يعني وسطها جعل عليها فضول السندس والاستبرق

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r8.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r8.claim: Anas reports that the Sidrah's fruit was like locusts and its leaves like elephant ears; when God's command covered it, it became ruby, emerald, and the like.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r8.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: انتهيت إلى السدرة فإذا نبقها مثل الجراد وإذا ورقها مثل آذان الفيلة

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r9.claim: Mujahid calls the Sidrah the first day of the Hereafter and the last day of this world, the point where things end.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {سدرة المنتهى} قال: أول يوم من الآخرة وآخر يوم من الدنيا فهو حيث ينتهي

DURR-FULL:v7p649/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r10.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r10.claim: Asma reports the Prophet's description of a vast Sidrah whose shade extends for a hundred years of travel, with golden moths and fruit like large jars.
DURR-FULL:v7p649/r10.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصف سدرة المنتهى قال: يسير الراكب في الفتن منها مائة سنة

DURR-FULL:v7p650/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Sidrah's branches were pearl and ruby; Muhammad saw it with his heart and saw his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p650/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {إذ يغشى السدرة ما يغشى} قال: كان أغصان السدرة من لؤلؤ وياقوت وقد رآها محمد بقلبه ورأى ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.claim: The account advances from denied earthly sight to a greater sight in the upper realm, moving upward through the manifestations of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p99/r7.anchor: أي إن كنتم تجحدون رؤيته جبريل في الأرض فلقد رآه رؤية أعظم منها إذ رآه في العالم العلوي مصاحبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r2.claim: ‘At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary’ attaches to ‘he saw him.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r2.anchor: وقوله : { عند سدرة المنتهى } متعلق ب { رءاه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r3.claim: The tree is singled out for the place's honor, its great signs, and its place as the endpoint of ascent through ranks of honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r3.anchor: وخصت بالذكر رؤيته عند سدرة المنتهى لعظيم شرف المكان بما حصل عنده من آيات ربه الكبرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r4.claim: The name denotes a celestial place above the seventh heaven, explicitly mentioned in sound Miʿrāj reports from Companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r4.anchor: و { سدرة المنتهى } : اسم أطلقه القرآن على مكان علوي فوق السماء السابعة ، وقد ورد التصريح بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r5.speaker: جمع من الصحابة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r5.claim: Sound Miʿrāj reports from a group of Companions explicitly mention the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r5.anchor: حديث المعراج من الصحاح عن جمع من الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r6.claim: The name may liken the place to a branching lote tree or mark a boundary no angel passed; perhaps boundaries were conventionally marked with lote trees.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r6.anchor: ولعله شبه ذلك المكان بالسدرة التي هي واحدة شجر السدر إما في صفة تفرعه ، وإما في كونه حدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r7.claim: The genitive may be explanatory, or define the tree by the endpoint it marks, beyond which creatures cannot endure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r7.anchor: وإضافة { سدرة } إلى { المنتهى } يجوز أن تكون إضافة بيانية . ويجوز كونها لتعريف السدرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r8.claim: Sidr is the lote tree, said to have deep shade, delicious fruit, and sweet fragrance; it likens this place as the palm likens a believer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p100/r8.anchor: والسدرة : واحدة السدر وهو شجر النبق قالوا : ويختص بثلاثة أوصاف : ظل مديد ، وطعم لذيذ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r4.claim: In the Miʿrāj report, the Prophet heard the pens' scratching, and God prescribed fifty prayers for his community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r4.anchor: ففي حديث الإسراء ( حتى ظهرت بمستوى أسمع فيه صريف الأقلام ففرض الله على أمتي خمسين صلاة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r5.claim: The Prophet received revelation directly from God without the angel as intermediary, honoring him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p101/r5.anchor: وما حصل فيه للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم من التشريف بتلقي الوحي مباشرة من الله دون واسطة الملك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r11.claim: The Sidrat al-Muntahā is a lote tree; Kaʿb places it in the seventh heaven, as in Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa’s Prophetic report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r11.anchor: و: سدرة المنتهى هي شجرة نبق، قال كعب: هي في السماء السابعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd places the lote tree in the sixth heaven.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r12.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: في السماء السادسة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r13.claim: One explanation of its name is that created knowledge ends there, beyond which only God knows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r13.anchor: لأنها إليها ينتهي علم كل عالم، ولا يعلم ما وراءها صعدا إلا الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r14.claim: Another explanation is that those who die following the Prophet’s Sunna reach it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies them as true believers in every generation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r14.anchor:
لأنها إليها ينتهي من مات على سنة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.
قال القاضي أبو محمد: هم المؤمنون حقا من كل جيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r15.claim: Another explanation says descending commands are received there and do not pass beyond it, while what ascends from earth is received there by the lower angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r15.anchor: لأن ما نزل من أمر الله فعندها يتلقى ولا يتجاوزها ملائكة العلو، وما صعد من الأرض فعندها يتلقى ولا يتجاوزها ملائكة السفل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r16.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r16.claim: The Prophet said a community among the communities would shelter in the shade of one of its branches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r16.anchor: وروي عن النبي عليه السلام أن الأمة من الأمم تستظل بظل الفنن منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r17.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r17.claim: The Prophet described its fruits as large as the jars of Hajar and its leaves as large as elephant ears.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#3/r17.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «رفعت لي سدرة المنتهى، فإذا نبقها مثل قلال هجر، وإذا ورقها مثل آذان الفيلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r1.claim: The continuation of the Prophetic description says colors covered the lote tree, whose nature the Prophet did not know.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p200/r1.anchor: فغشيها ألوان لا أدري ما هي؟

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r5.claim: The sidra is the lote tree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r5.anchor: فأما سدرة المنتهى فالسدرة شجرة النبق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r6.claim: A sound Prophetic report describes its fruit as jars from Hajar and its leaves as elephant ears; Ibn al-Jawzī explicitly calls the report sound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r6.anchor: وقد صح في الحديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال نبقها مثل قلال هجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r7.speaker: مالك بن صعصعة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r7.claim: One view places the tree above the seventh heaven, supported by the report of Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections; Muqātil places it to the right of the Throne.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r7.anchor: أحدهما أنها فوق السماء السابعة وهذا مذكور في الصحيحين من حديث مالك بن صعصعة قال مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r8.claim: A second view places the tree in the sixth heaven, reported in Muslim’s individual narration from Ibn Masʿūd and also held by al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r8.anchor: والثاني أنها في السماء السادسة أخرجه مسلم في أفراده عن ابن مسعود وبه قال الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r9.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r9.claim: The exegetes say it is the limit where what rises from earth and what descends from above is received, and where the angels’ knowledge ends.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p68#3/r9.anchor: وإليها ينتهي ما يهبط به من فوقها فيقبض منها وإليها ينتهي علم جميع الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.claim: This is the second time Muhammad saw Gabriel in his created form, on the Night Journey; Ibn Kathir says earlier Isra reports already supply the details.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p451/r3.anchor: هذه هي المرة الثانية التي رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها جبريل على صورته التي خلقه الله عليها، وكانت ليلة الإسراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports seeing Gabriel at the Lote Tree with six hundred wings; Asim would not explain their span, while some of his companions said a wing stretched from east to west. Ibn Kathir calls the chain good.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r2.claim: Another good-chain report from Ibn Masud says Gabriel came wearing greenery adorned with pearls.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p452/r2.anchor: أتاني جبريل، عليه السلام، في خضر معلق به الدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r5.claim: Earlier Night Journey reports say angels like ravens, the Lord's light, and unidentifiable colors covered the Lote Tree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r5.anchor: قد تقدم في أحاديث الإسراء أنه غشيتها الملائكة مثل الغربان، وغشيها نور الرب، وغشيها ألوان ما أدري ما هي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r6.claim: Ibn Masud places the Lote Tree in the seventh heaven, where what ascends from earth and descends from above ends; it was covered by golden moths. The Prophet received the five prayers, the closing verses of al-Baqara, and forgiveness for major sins among those who avoid shirk; Ibn Kathir says Muslim alone transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r6.anchor: عن مرة، عن عبد الله-هو ابن مسعود-قال: لما أسري برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انتهي به إلى سدرة المنتهى، وهي في السماء السابعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة أو غيره (شك أبو جعفر الرازي)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r7.claim: Abu Ja'far is unsure whether the authority was Abu Hurayra or another; the report says divine light and ravenlike angels covered the Tree, then God spoke to the Prophet and told him to ask.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r7.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي هريرة أو غيره -شك أبو جعفر-قال: لما أسري برسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r8.claim: Mujahid says the Tree's branches were pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and that Muhammad saw it and saw his Lord with his heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p453/r8.anchor: وقال (5) ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {إذ يغشى السدرة ما يغشى} قال: كان أغصان السدرة لؤلؤا وياقوتا وزبرجدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود (على ظن محمد)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.claim: A report tentatively attributed to Ibn Masud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice: once when requested, when Gabriel filled the horizon, and again on the ascent. Gabriel then returned to his form and prostrated; the great signs were Gabriel's creation. Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Kathir calls it strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.anchor: قال محمد: أظنه عن ابن مسعود -أنه قال: إن محمدا لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

JISHUMI:v9p6640/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r11.claim: Al-muntahā is where one arrives and beyond which one does not pass.
JISHUMI:v9p6640/r11.anchor: والمنتهى: التي ينتهى إليها فلا يتجاوز عنها
